definitions.explanation: Water that has been heated, as opposed to cold water.

examples.japanese: お{湯|ゆ}を{沸|わ}かしてください。
カップラーメンにお{湯|ゆ}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Pour hot water into the cup noodles.

examples.japanese: お{湯|ゆ}が{熱|あつ}すぎるので、{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
examples.english: The water is too hot, so please wait a moment.

notes:
お{湯|ゆ} is the polite/everyday word for hot water. The お prefix is honorific but is almost always used; {湯|ゆ} alone sounds old-fashioned or literary.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{湯|ゆ}を{沸|わ}かす (to boil water)
- お{湯|ゆ}を{入|い}れる (to pour/add hot water)
- お{湯|ゆ}が{出|で}る (hot water comes out)
- お{湯|ゆ}に{入|はい}る (to take a bath)

RELATED WORDS:
- {水|みず} (cold water)
- {温|ぬる}い (lukewarm)
- {熱|あつ}い (hot)

NOTE: In bath contexts, お{湯|ゆ}に{入|はい}る means 'to take a bath' (literally 'to enter the hot water').
